label: <DEL> step when the sequence starts with u/q/2/t (first token to recall)
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step (98% of activations, 99% of mass), where the model must output original token 0. It barely fires during the original or later copy phases. Within the delimiter step it is set by which token is being recalled first: rate is about 51% when the first token is u, about 40% for q, 2 and t, falls off through e, p, j, z, g, k, 1, and is near zero for most other tokens. The top activations are all sequences starting with u, q, 2 or t. The second original token (next_out) also pushes it up, with u, q, z, t and e helping, so the response looks like a graded sum over the first one or two tokens rather than a crisp set. Sequence length has little effect. phase==1 alone gives recall 0.98 but precision 0.13. Restricting first_tok to {u,q,2,t} gives F1 about 0.53 and mass recall about 0.66. Conjunctions with the second token did not improve on that.
